crash.title: Markets are crashing
crash.story: Shares have fallen about {pct}% this year and your funds went down with them. The news is full of people getting out.
gut: A small voice wonders whether to sell.
Your stomach is turning. Selling feels sensible.
Your gut is screaming: get out now, before it gets worse!

follow.title: Sell my shares
follow.blurb: Move all your shares into fixed deposits at today's low prices. Tax applies on any gain.

resist.title: Hold on
resist.blurb: Stay invested and wait it out.

raise.title: A big raise
raise.story: The new pay is a big step up. Time to treat yourself: a bigger flat, a better car, nicer holidays?
gut: You could do with a few small treats.
You have earned a proper upgrade, surely.
Your gut says: new car, new flat, new everything!

follow.title: Upgrade my life
follow.blurb: Everyday costs go up by about a fifth, for good.

resist.title: Carry on as before
resist.blurb: Keep your lifestyle and bank the difference.

festival.title: Festival season
festival.story: Diwali is coming. Everyone is shopping, gifting and dressing up, and the offers are everywhere.
gut: A little gift here and there would be nice.
It is only once a year, after all.
Your gut says: go big, buy everything, gift everyone!

follow.title: Splurge
follow.blurb: Spend about 5% of a year's pay on the celebrations.

tip.title: A hot tip
tip.story: A friend swears a small company is about to take off, and they have already put money in. 'Get in now,' they say.
gut: It sounds risky. You are not tempted.
It does sound interesting, and everyone seems to be in.
Your gut says: this is the big one. Do not miss out!

follow.title: Put money in
follow.blurb: Stake a tenth of your savings. Most tips like this lose the lot; a few pay several times over.

resist.title: Pass
resist.blurb: Keep your savings where they are.

provenance.basis: Game design, not data. A card can appear after a year in which it applies, at most two a stage (the crash card always appears and does not count). Crash: shares fell at least 15% in the year and you hold at least 1 lakh of them. Raise: after a recruiter's offer, with a chance of 30% plus your lifestyle creep. Festival: 8% plus a fifth of your lifestyle creep each year. Hot tip: 4% plus a tenth of how little cautious you are. Following the crash card sells all your shares into fixed deposits at that point; a raise adds a fifth to everyday costs for good; a festival costs 5% of pay; a tip stakes 10% of your sellable savings and returns three times the stake in one case in five. The stakes and payoff are made up to show the pattern (the expected result is a loss), not drawn from data.
